messages:
acme-ops: Hey team, after rotating our key we started getting 401 invalid_api_key on every request. We rotated the key via the console and updated our docker-compose env var, but the service still fails. No other changes.

Maria S.: Thanks for the report. Can you paste the request youre sending (headers redacted except the auth header)? Also confirm whether youre using Authorization: Bearer or X-API-Key.

acme-ops: Were using Authorization: Bearer. Here's the curl we run from inside the container (I replaced the token with <REDACTED>):

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

acme-ops: The token in the container env looks shorter than the one in the console. So maybe something truncated it when we updated compose.

Jon (SRE): How are you populating the env var in docker-compose? Common pitfall is not quoting values with $ or other shell metacharacters so Compose (or shell) expands them. Example YAML problem:

```yaml
services:
  app:
    environment:
      - REDWOOD_API_KEY=$MY_KEY_FROM_VAULT
```

If MY_KEY contains a $ or other sequence, or if you rely on the shell to expand, you can end up with a different value or an empty one.

acme-ops: Ah! We pull the key into the CI env and set REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_KEY in the compose file. The real key has a literal "$" in it (part of the rotation output).

Eli (Engine): Yep thats the cause. The shell is trying to expand $... and either replaces it with nothing or with a different var. Two quick fixes: 1) use quotes in the compose file: "REDWOOD_API_KEY='${REDWOOD_KEY}'" or 2) set the env var from the environment without inline interpolation, e.g. in compose v2 use:

```yaml
environment:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${REDWOOD_KEY}
```

Or export the var in the shell before running docker-compose.

acme-ops: We applied quotes and restarted the container. Requests now succeed. Thanks!

Maria S.: Great — glad that worked. For the record, we also accept keys in the X-API-Key header if you prefer to avoid Authorization header differences: `X-API-Key: <key>`

Jon (SRE): Leaving a quick repro snippet in case anyone else hits this:

```bash
# bad (will expand $ inside the key)
docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$ROTATED_KEY myapp
# good (preserve literal value)
docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY="$ROTATED_KEY" myapp
```

Maria S.: Ill close the support ticket since the customer confirmed resolution. Leaving a note: cause=unquoted-env-with-dollar, resolution=quote-or-use-compose-var, followup=docs link update.

support-bot: Ticket #23412 moved to Resolved by Maria S. :white_check_mark:
